title: Logopedic self-intervention program in voice therapy
summary:
Background
Patients with speech, language, swallowing, or voice disorders are increasingly facing longer waiting times for therapy. This is primarily due to a shortage of specialists. An increase in voice disorders has also been observed in recent years. Self-intervention programs (SIP) could be a suitable measure to overcome this supply bottleneck. However, there is still no reliable data available on whether voice therapy with an increased self-learning component is as effective as the regular voice therapy.
 
The aim is to examine whether self-learning programs in voice therapy are inferior to the standard of care. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of voice therapy with a self-learning component on the voice as well as the motivation and satisfaction of patients. In addition, the factors for the success of self-learning in voice therapy are to be identified.

Methods
The experimental phoniatrics department of the ENT clinic and the Institute for General and Palliative Medicine are collaborating on a program that enables patients to undergo voice therapy treatment at home with the aid of video. A randomized, controlled intervention study with supplementary qualitative process evaluation (mixed-method design) will investigate whether the increased use of innovative therapeutic SIP programs in voice therapy is inferior to standard therapy. The process will be evaluated across all study arms using various methods.

Therapy with or without increased EL will be carried out over a period of 10 weeks. Four comparison groups will be formed. As part of the study, patients will receive voice therapy in individual sessions with a self-exercise program (group B.1, 5 individual sessions, 5 EL sessions), group therapy with a self-exercise program (group B.2, 5 group sessions, 5 EL sessions), or only a self-exercise program (group C, 10 EL sessions) with patients who are treated as before without an EL program. 

The primary endpoint is the Voice Handicap Index 30 (VHI-30). The VHI-30 is a self-assessment questionnaire that covers various aspects of a voice disorder. In addition, basic sociodemographic data of the participating patients and other voice parameters will be collected as secondary endpoints. Various aspects will be taken into account in the process evaluation of the intervention, including exercise frequency, training diaries, and the personal perspective of the patients. The perspective of the treating speech therapists will be collected through qualitative interviews.

interventions.name: Group A: Care as usual, 10 therapy sessions with a speech and language therapist in a 1:1 setting
Group B1: 5 therapy sessions 1:1 with a speech and language therapist, every second week self-intervention program (SIP)
Group B2: 5 therapy sessions  in a group setting with a speech and language therapist, every second week self-intervention program
Group C: 10 sessions of self-intervention program

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Language requirements for informed participation, answering questions, and undergoing therapy
• Medically diagnosed functional dysphonia
• Initial prescription for voice therapy (ST2)
• VHI-30 was administered
Exclusion criteria:
•  No functional voice disorder (e.g., organic cause)
•  Desire for therapy to transition the voice in trans patients
•   Already undergoing voice therapy treatment
•  Therapy for professional singers' voices
•  Non-consent
